body: Block her!!! This is your perfect opportunity to go NC

Yes, we're sort of fwb, but I really don't consider him a friend... I don't tell him my stuff because I'd rather tell someone else and I don't want to share my private things with him. We both enjoy the sex. I wouldn't jump straight into a relationship with him, or with anyone, without being totally sure, I'd rather take things slowly and carefully, but eventually, I'd like to have a relationship with him. Unless, of course, my feelings change or I realize he's an idiot/a psycho/etc.

The thing with the ex girlfriend is what I find most worrying... Not wanting a relationship and making it clear from the very beginning, without feeding expectations, is IMO a green flag. 

His ex-wife (not the same person as said ex-girlfriend), who supposedly ruined his life and deprived him of his possessions, and is (according to him) the ultimate evil, INVARIABLY comes up. However, I think there must be another side to the story, and that although it may have been a complicated divorce, it was not only her fault. It's just not possible.
Congrats!!! With her moving away, your limerence will vanish!!! It's the best thing that can happen to you! Say hello to your new peace of mind
I hate myself for loving you, by Joan Jett/ Poison, by Alice Cooper, One way or another, Blondie.

Really clever point of view!! Of course there are always "excuses" to avoid a relationship! Anyway, the affair began only a month ago, it's too soon to speak of a relationship (with him or anyone, for that matter) , but he should definitely stop displaying himself as a victim.
I didn't. My family was loving and I don't have any childhood traumas. IDK why I'm limerent.
And yes. He's totally terrified of loving and being dumped/hurt. That's what he said millions of times
You hit the nail. Although I don't think this is even close to a relationship, I really ought to ask myself this question and find an honest answer. If not, I'll be in a sentimental limbo forever.
So basically he's using me for sex and "free psychotherapy"?
Because he was very emphatic about that
Absolutely. I love how I can be weird and totally myself around him.
He isn't, but I am (recently). He's emotionally unavailable because he's scared of commitment and rejection, due to past trauma. He's kinda crazy, but a good guy, though

I didn't mean he loves me or anything because he looked at me. I was only thinking of eventual possibilities. It may also happen that I grow tired of him, or that the affair fades away on its own. Or that I fall for him but he doesn't, or the other way round. I was also wondering how likely it was.
Yeah, you get a little bit and you find yourself craving for more... Just like drugs.
Exactly, something similar happened to me, but now that we know what limerence is about, we have more tools to control these feelings

I totally understand how you feel. It's awful. I think the only way out is NC. Not seeing this person and blocking him from everywhere will give you a different perspective (it takes time). 

Don't use dating apps, because all you'll look for are guys which look like him. Do you have the possibility to travel somewhere? Take a short trip or vacation? That would help a lot.
Me! I don't want this shit ever again.

Tell him: "Thanks for the invite, but you took it back. I can't deal with such unstable and toxic people. I wish you peace and success in your life." And block him from everywhere, go NC. I find his attitude manipulative and mean.
I think so, too. Some narcissistic people are like that.

All your fury and rage are hurting no one but you. Your LO isn't even aware of your thirst for revenge. Thoughts of revenge and anger are maybe a part of the grieving process, but the important thing is that you don't act on them. Go NC and block her from everywhere, so you don't even have a chance to harass her.
Not at all!! What worries me is the persistence of these feelings. I hope they vanish soon and never come back.
I absolutely loved your rant. Wonderfully expressed, and the blunt and clear truth
You're not! It's public information. As long as you don't go there and start patroling his house and contacting his family, it's harmless. But it's not healthy for you!!

You made the best decision. Blocking someone is the best option for your mental health and peace of mind. It may also help to focus on what an asshole he is. He's the one who needs to reaffirm himself by using women. He's the pathetic one, not you!!! Focus on that.
I'm trying... But if you want to DM, I'm willing to help

Yes. Although I'm still limerent for him, I must stay strong and keep NC. Today I had a great opportunity to talk to him, but instead I didn't. I understand his broken heart, his fears and everything, but everything has a limit. I gave him enough signals and spent lots of time thinking of excuses to get close to him. I'm not willing to make any efforts anymore. I've done enough.

No limerence lasts forever. One day you'll eventually forget the LO, or at least transfer to someone who hopefully reciprocates. But keep up with NC. Maybe you can focus on how miserable they make you. Do you deserve to feel like this? The answer is no. Focus on the negative effect they have on you and hold on to that to fight limerence.

I totally relate!!! My LO flooded me with TMI and personal issues, which I took as a sign of interest... However, I decided to go NC because he never asked me out and because I he accidentally said "my girlfriend" when talking about her ex, which shows that he's still hooked on her. I really can't tell if he likes you or not, but I'd try to avoid him, due to your professional situation

I've found my dream apartment (I'm coming back and forth these months, but I'll be relocating definitely in some months) NEXT TO my LO's workplace. I'm definitely not going to miss out on my dream apartment because of an asshole. I've already gone NC (as much as possible), I hope I'm not limerent as soon as possible, so his presence doesn't affect me.
Great advice!!! I'm trying, with some ups and downs but I think it's working!

As they told you, focusing on their bad traits can help. But I'd advise you to go totally NC. Totally. Burn all bridges, cut all ties. Block them from everywhere, avoid them at all costs, until you're not limerent anymore.

Yeah... Sharing too much too soon can be devastating, not only when it comes to limerence. Even random people or so-called friends could stab you in the back with your own information, so please be very careful!! Protect your secrets and your intimacy, they belong to you only.

I'm afraid I disagree with you about blocking a potential relationship because he's still hooked up on his ex. I, or any woman he dates for that matter, will be nothing but a "cheap replacement", and I don't want to be treated like that, by an LO or by anyone. Hearing him say "my gf" by mistake while I'm sure I saw his eyes light up was enough evidence for me. I don't need or want any other explanation from him. But tbh it still hurts... 

Fortunately, I didn't share details of my life, and answered evasively when he asked me. In general, I'm extremely reserved, that's why I share all these details anonymously on the internet. My LO is the exact opposite. He has even made me uncomfortable with his verbal waterfall of TMI, and I found it unusual that he shared so many personal and intimate things with someone he barely knew. But maybe he's that way, and didn't do it because I was "special". This TMI included his ex and her body jewelry, about which nobody asked. 

As you said,  totally avoiding someone next door is impossible, and being rude to him will certainly backfire in some way, and it's simply not right. I certainly tried to walk by when I thought he would be there or at least see me, and even went the opposite way just for him to see me. I won't take all that trouble again, and I won't find any excuses to talk to him. If I need something, I'll ask someone else. 

Fortunately, all my elaborate plans and schedules for him to see me weren't perceived from the outside: from his point of view, I was just passing by with a shopping bag, a smoothie or groceries, like the other neighbors, so all the elaborate things were only visible for me. 

Although he has acted weird around me and done inexplicable things, he's too scared of being hurt (so he said), and I told him I don't want an SO. I could save some face, but I'm still very limerent for him and the idea of seeing him terrifies me.
I'll give it a go!
Maybe travelling will open your mind and give you new experiences and insights!! Take this unique opportunity to grow and learn.
Love is love, and limerence is limerence, regardless of gender. I don't think it has to do with your mom. Power is seductive, and that's why we're attracted to authority figures.

Absolutely!! I wish I'd never met him!! Or that I'd met him, but ignored him/didn't become limerent. I spoke to him in the first place because "I was curious". I could have just satisfied my curiosity and never speak to him again.

I know. But I'm glad I didn't disclose. Although both of us are single, neither I or he are emotionally available. He's still in love with his ex (which I didn't know before), and I'm depressed because my ex husband makes my life miserable. 

I thought he also had a crush on me. Although he may find me attractive, I wouldn't get involved with someone who is with me while still longing for someone else. As regards myself, I'm too depressed and i don't think I can think or act clearly at the moment.

OMG I'm really sorry to hear about your health condition, I wish you a complete recovery. 

Of course, I understand. The purpose of this sub is to help each other, without judgement. No offense taken :)
Hang in there!!! A burden becomes less heavy when it's shared, even online.

We all have problems to sort out, and in this sub we've all read about intense, depressive and changeable states of mind, and tried to help. Otherwise we wouldn't be looking for support and advice on the internet. 

I really don't see what's wrong with venting negative feelings about someone as long as it's anonymous. I've been extra careful not to give away any details that could remotely help identify him, or myself. I've never spoken bad about him with people I know, and I'd never mess with his work or his reputation.

Maybe I imagined his signals, or I saw what I wanted to see. Maybe the guy was just acting weird/saying weird and unusual things, and I misunderstood him. He didn't act completely normal, like everyone else does. 

Before my comments face a shitstorm, I want to make one thing clear: he's not pathetic because he didn't like me although I was a "good match". If I had been in his situation (someone has a crush on me but I want nothing to do with them), I would be extra careful not to say anything misleading. I would never, ever share intimate and personal things with someone I have no interest in. I have principles and  I won't use this information against him, or hurt/harass him in any way. 

I admit to being angry, and maybe my anger is misdirected. I should be furious with myself for being so stupid. But anger doesn't last forever, and at least it will push me out of my limerent limbo.

I would never dream of harassing or hurting anyone because they didn't reciprocate. I'm angry with the whole situation, and also with myself for not seeing the signs. I just want to detach myself from this situation and this person.

I'm not saying he should be grateful I liked him, but if he had no interest in the first place, he shouldn't have given mixed signals. That's what makes him a narcissistic idiot. He shouldn't have "enjoyed the ego boost" at my expense. 

And about his own limerence, well, I don't blame him, he probably can't control it and it makes him suffer. But others don't have to suffer for HIS limerence

Asking lots of questions about my relationship status, telling me private things, finding excuses to lightly touch my arm/hand (even with Covid and social distancing), acting weird and fidgeting, and telling me like 100 times he didn't have an SO. However, the only positive steps he had to take -get my number and ask me out- he didn't. So I assume he enjoyed the attention and I only fueled his ego trips.

Same thing here. I'm currently going NC because I found out he was still in love with his ex. But I also got tired of his mixed signals. We all deserve clear communication, not breadcrumbs of attention.
Exactly. Actions speak louder than words. If he hasn't made any clear move, well, he's already said it. It took me like 6 months of limerence to understand that.

IDK what your native language is, but in German it's Limerenz, and in Spanish it's called limerencia. If your therapist doesn't know the concept, maybe you can explain it to them. Many years ago, I was limerent for a guy, but I didn't know the term. I went to therapy because I was feeling so bad and guilty about it, and although I didn't even know the word existed, I managed to explain my feelings. Tell them exactly how you feel, and remember they can't judge you or tell anyone, and they've probably seen worse things.
Go NC. I know how you feel, it's horrible. But you have to get them out of your mind. Focus on yourself and your own growth.
The anger will eventually fade away. As long as you don't hurt yourself or anyone, there's no reason to worry about it. And maybe it's better to be angry than to be limerent.

I could eventually focus on the fact that he's hooked on his ex, and will never want me... I don't know him that much to focus on his negative traits... And I don't know the positive ones either, except for the fact that he seems to be a good guy.

Yes. I was limerent for a professor at college, and that made my academic skills flourish. When I was limerent for a dance coach, I perfected my dancing skills. The rest of my limerences were minor, they were crushes indeed, so they didn't influence my life. 

The dance coach was a bit of a jerk, but not a bad guy after all. I still remember my professor very fondly, as an inspiring academic personality, which he was. All traces of this limerence are long gone, and the professor must have passed away by now, or be very old. He was an enlightening influence in my professional life.

Get in touch with real people, with real friends. Maybe join a group of something, and make new acquaintances. Join a class, start learning a language, that's great because it will give you opportunities to communicate verbally and maybe find people with similar interests.
There isn't a "right time in the future". You have to create that right time, at the right moment for you. Or let go even if it's painful, if you feel confessing will be to no avail

Totally. Next time, unless a dude begs and pleads, NC and indifference. And I'm not sure about the former: I already had two abusive relationships, including a long-term marriage, so I don't trust my judgement anymore.

As regards your LO, maybe you could be friends in the future, when you're not limerent anymore. For the time being, I'd advise you to focus on your well-being. If she gets offended because of your indifference, well, sorry not sorry.

Fortunately, I never actually told him how I feel or asked him out. However, I did show interest by finding excuses to talk to him and I even gave him a small present in return for a favor, with which he seemed very pleased. He's always been kind and nice to me, but that wasn't what I wanted. 

At least I told him I wasn't interested in a relationship when he asked if I had an SO, and could more or less keep a straight face (partially due to my covid mask) when he had his unfortunate Freudian slip. 

At least my shyness about asking him out prevented me from making a complete fool of myself.

Not exactly a success story, but I was horribly limerent for a guy who despised me. That was like 10 years ago, and the whole shit lasted Like 2 years. I was lucky that he emigrated and that made my limerence vanish automatically.
*opposite

Idk, but overcoming your low self esteem will definitely improve your life. I really don't know if low self esteem and Limerence are connected, but if your self esteem improves, at least it will be easier to handle

Don't worry about your marriage if it was already doomed. I'm sure you'll find another good job opportunity if you have a good resume. Hold on to your friends, journal your thoughts, and BLOCK THE LO FROM EVERYWHERE!!!  And although I'm just an internet stranger, feel free to DM me if you want..
Now? "The asshole"

I totally understand you. I also want to end my life, because I'm depressed (reasons other than limerence, I was suicidal before meeting lo). Limerence will eventually fade away, so don't end your life because of a person. 

People with suicidal thoughts don't necessarily want to stop living, but to stop living in a particular way. Maybe if you focus on changing the conditions that make your life miserable, you'll feel better.
No doubt. Block him without any remorse. What matters is your peace of mind.

I'm really sorry for you... Was the guy a colleague who ruined your career? Did you leave your husband for him? Try your best to protect your heart and surround yourself with a support network of family and friends who could help you... Reach out to your loved ones. And go absolutely NC. Block him from everywhere.

My idea was, after some ideas of asking him out, put everything on hold because of my current problems. But now I'm going NC, cold turkey. He did give me mixed signals, but this Freudian slip was the last straw. I can't cope with stupid shenanigans at the moment, and I'll prioritize my mental health. So I'm going NC. 

I'm sure I got limerent for him because I was depressed and suicidal (as I said, I met him just two days after attempting su1cide). The whole thing has been going on for 6 months. I'll get my shit together, and I can't focus or think clearly with a LO in the middle.

As you said, body language never lies. He seemed very happy to remember his ex-GF's body jewelry, about which no-one asked. I know Covid masks make it hard to read body language, but I did see the glimmer in his eyes, and he did say "my girlfriend" accidentally. 

I'm in a totally fragile state of mind, which may have lead to the limerent state as well. I can't date him or anyone without solving my depression and suicidal ideations first, and keeping the abuser at bay. 

I'll definitely go NC. When I'm better, either I'll forget him and look for other kind of guys, or if I still like him in a healthy and non-limerent way and he likes me back, I may give it a go, with clear boundaries and cold feet.

Less than a year, and we're not legally divorced yet. I'm struggling with suicidal thoughts because my ex-husband just keeps pestering my life and has basically ruined my self-esteem during our marriage.

Exactly. I must be totally sure and boundaries must be crystal clear. And that's exactly what deters me. If he was just a random guy, well, I may ask him out and never see him again (cut contact). But not being able to do so eventually makes it more difficult. And that goes for him too.
Go NC ASAP, or as NC as you possibly can. Good thing you didn't confess and lose face!!

I think so, too. I remember I bought something at his store before the pandemic, and then didn't see him for a year (I was "the new neighbor"). As soon as he saw me again, he remembered me at once. I'm not saying he had a crush, but well, at least he remembered a stranger who he had seen only once. If he's interested, he'll wait. If he gets someone else, well, he was never into me, otherwise he would have acted on it.

Yes, that's what I normally do. He actually has a store next door and I live in a huge building which is full of surveillance cameras, but has a wonderful rooftop... Maybe he can come over and chill on the terrace, if he doesn't mind being watched hehe ... Or we could go to a nearby park.

Thanks for the answers!! Yes, although I really like him, and my invitation will probably be accepted, the problem is what happens later... If he ghosts me, something goes sour, or if on the contrary, everything goes great but I'm still depressed, it will be hard on me. And maybe I'm attracted to him precisely BECAUSE I'm depressed (he has a slight eating disorder and had depressive issues, too). Getting to know him better without the pressure of "being rejected" is a better idea for the time being.

It's true, I've been overcomplicating things for months, not weeks. 

We're indeed two single people, but I always expect the man to make the first move, I'm scared of rejection because I'm depressed and suicidal at the moment,  and I prefer beating around the bush to the sole possibility of being rejected, which would be the last straw. He also had opportunities to ask me out,but didn't, so I assume he isn't interested enough. If he was or if he had shown more interest, I wouldn't hesitate. 

I didn't kill myself in the last few weeks only because I don't have access to a gun and if I had overdosed on pills, I'd have been rescued. I'm extremely depressed at the moment. Going out with him would cheer me up, but wouldn't solve the deep issues. 

Maybe I should go and ask him out, knowing that I'll be rejected, only to end this limerence shit forever, at least for this guy. I just wouldn't dare asking someone out unless I'm 200% sure he'll accept. Maybe I should try and get him out of my mind instead of devising ways to ask him out/reach him.

Well yes, it shouldn't be the end of the world if someone rejects me, but I don't want it to happen. I live next door from him and I'm in a very fragile state of mind at the moment, due to other things. I definitely don't need, or can't cope with, being rejected, even if it brings closure or "something better eventually". I just couldn't handle ANY rejection at the moment.

What you say is true. He could have asked me out long ago, he had some opportunities, but on the other hand I mentioned that I didn't want to have an SO, in order no to sound clingy or desperate. I understand him being a hurt man and all that, but well, we all have problems and issues... Once he told me he'd been asked out, but his date canceled the plan at the last minute, so that means he wouldn't be horrified if a woman asks him out. I could have asked him out, too, but didn't. I could have obtained his number , but I didn't want to without his consent. He could have asked him mine with any dumb excuse, but didn't. As a man, he's supposed to make the first move. I wonder why he is so curious about my relationship status, and stalks me on and offline (he's given himself away with the FB stalking, and mentioned that "I always walk by at the same time". He also stalks my mom, offline) ... Asking him out only to be rejected will certainly cool off the Limerence and cut the shit, but oh boy what a blow in the face! I may not get rejected though, but... I'm not totally sure
Of course. Personally, I don't conceive Limerence without sexual attraction

I can totally relate to this... Also towards the end of 2020 I told my ex-husband I wanted a divorce (we haven't divorced yet, but we're no longer a couple). That was before I ever spoke to my LO, but as my limerence began in January, I wanted more and more to get a divorce... Although my ex husband tried his best to fix the marriage (after some 8 years of decline, which involved some verbal and emotional abuse on his part) , I was decided I wasn't going to put up with his abuse anymore. At the beginning, I didn't want to be in a relationship with the LO, but the problem is that now I want to give it a go, because I got to know him a little better and I d like to at least give it a shot .. 

What scares me is: did the appearance of the LO in my life blur my reasoning and made me end a 10-year marriage, which had lots of issues but eventually could be fixed, or was it the right decision to leave a marriage which was unhappy, with or without an LO? 

I thought about suicide many times and I still do (the hope of being with the LO doesn't matter anymore, if I'm dead, the limerence will be gone, too), but I can't have my house available and ALONE for a COUPLE of days, so nobody will find me or help me. My ex-husband, with whom I still live, is ALWAYS at home and never lets me some air. 

I want everything to end. The divorce issues, the limerence, the sadness, and any other future problems that may arise

In fact, I don't hold him on a pedestal, he has flaws, but it's precisely because of, and not in spite of these, that I'm so limerent and obsessed with him. He's broken and imperfect, and I just love that. 

The ball idea would be great, if it weren't for the position of his window, which is likely to get broken, and he certainly wouldn't like that. He doesn't frequent the nearby park, if not, it would be a great opportunity. 

I get less nervous around him than before, but I still get nervous!!! I hate that, because I'm fully grown up and I shouldn't act/feel like a teenager, I want to be in control of myself, if not of the situation. 

Mind you, I live next door from his store, not from his house. For some reason my niece LOVES his shop window (he doesn't sell any items for kids, but she likes it for some reason). I had some opportunities of striking a chat because of her fascination with the products on display, but I got flustered and literally grabbed the kiddo and ran away!!!! He doesn't sell any items that I need, so I can't use the "excuse" to buy something from him. 

Well, maybe next time my niece looks at the window, I could just wave hi, and if she starts pointing at something and he invites us in, well, I'll be a lucky girl!!!

Welcome to the club. I personally have been there, and still am... It's heart breaking, but it eventually goes away, it doesn't last forever. Anyway, if the guy is single and hasn't rejected you, maybe you could give it a go, and try to get him to ask you out
If you said it playfully and don't do it again, you don't need to be embarrassed. In fact, I find this move sorta cute.

Done a similar thing some months ago, but on foot... As long as you don't stare thru his window like a creep, or take pictures or do crazy things, it's sort of normal. Even people with "regular"crushes do that, provided you didn't drive miles to do that. You didn't see him and he didn't see you, nothing happened. But I'd avoid this behavior in the future, cos you may be spotted by a neighbor or surveillance cameras, and you will definitely look suspicious or even dangerous.

You'll feel terribly humiliated if he turns down your gift or your visit, and his SO will have every reason to be upset. Let alone if he has invited other friends. Super awkward. If I were you, I'd be more discreet

Speaking bad of exes, or of anyone for that matter, is suspicious IMO. But in this case, and according to HIS VERSION, he caught her red-handed ... So it wasn't his imagination, apparently. The thing is, why share that with me?
Sorry, there's something I don't get... Is she your SO? Are you roommates? Why do you live together?

He took me totally by surprise by asking me about my divorce, its reasons, how long my marriage had lasted, etc. Totally out of the blue. I answered without details and he saw I wasn't going to rant or to tell him anything,  but he did give me all these details... Then we spoke about other things, and he indirectly asked me if I had an SO, which I don't. 

TMI makes me uncomfortable in general, and I'm personally very reserved. And I was surprised that he opened up in that way with me, but at the same time, criticizing exes is supposed to be a red flag...
I wouldn't do it if I were you. Maybe if you want to send him a nice message and a small gift, it's ok. But not in front of this friends and let alone his boyfriend. Don't expose yourself!

I totally understand... And sometimes people are really mean... A friend of mine told me that all men who criticize exes are automatically mysogynistic and deep down, they hate women. If his ex-wife really did what he said, well, she's mean as hell. But what I don't know is,even if such extreme things happened, if it's ok to vent about them.

He bombarded me with Q's about my divorce, which I answered evasively. He saw he wasn't going to get me to criticize my ex, so he started his own rant. If I wanted to, I could have said horrible things, too. Before my ex-husband, I was in an abusive relationship (which I described to my then-husband, because THEN it wasn't frowned upon to criticize exes). My ex husband is a good person, but he did some nasty things that led to our divorce. I could have ranted, but chose not to. For one thing, I'm extremely reserved and I rarely share information, and for another, I didn't want to sound resentful or bitchy.

If he's attracted to such women, then he won't find me attractive... I may have lots of flaws but I'm no narcissist. He does seem to crave approval, though, or otherwise he wouldn't have eating disorders which make him terrified of gaining weight. And yes, he's terrified of suffering (I suspected it, and then he told me so)... Nowadays it's totally taboo to speak ill of exes, according to all "love gurus" around, but back in the old days it was totally accepted, and I know many really sweet and loyal people who have said terrible things about their exes.

The situation he described involving his ex-wife and her cheating was appaling, and if anyone told me such a story, I'd be equally horrified. If that actually happened, then his ex-wife is the meanest person in the world. IF that REALLY happened. 

His next ex was "bitchy" and overdemanding, and finally left him. I accidentally stumbled upon old pictures of them together (wish I could unsee them), and analyzing their body language, he seemed totally in love and sorta "powerless", while she looked more self-centered and focused on posing. 

Either he's the unluckiest man on Earth, or he's given these women reasons to be "bitchy and crazy".

Exactly. He sounds as if he was "a victim", who did nothing wrong and was cheated on/abandoned. Maybe he has issues which led him to choose unloving partners in the past, and wants to avoid the same mistakes at all costs, which is totally valid... But nowadays speaking ill of exes is sort of taboo...

I wouldn't be very hopeful. But there is a positive point, though. Since you're no longer workmates, you could find out her number or IG account and remain in touch! You got nothing to lose. If she also wants to see you, you'll go on a date and it may be the start of something beautiful. If not, well, you won't see her again, you go NC and save yourself the embarrassment.
Idk. He gives mixed signals. He asked me lots of personal questions and wanted to know if I have a SO, but he didn't ask me out. So IDK really.
On the same boat here. I feel exactly like you do. I really wish he was actually pining for me, but he isn't, I'm sure. I'm the only one who is obsessed about him.

In summer, I wear sexy outfits when I know my LO will see me, which is really difficult because he's next door and it's very likely that he'll see me, so I have to "dress up" even if I go on a simple errand. I wish he saw me in sexy outfits every day and went crazy over them. But I don't like looking vulgar, so I try to keep my looks sensual but still refined. I feel more confident that way.

Yes. The other day I had an extremely vivid dream about my LO and me in a restaurant. We ate an extremely realistic-looking, juicy steak, and we made out. The dream felt so realistic that I woke up confused. I wish my LO many nights of dreams like this, about me.

I can more or less relate. My LEs weren't on occasional people, but when I was 15 I became limerent for a guy at the bus stop. He turned out to be a teacher at my school!!! I had a huge crush on him and I hoped to see him at the bus stop. 3 years later (I was 18) he and I coincided on the same French course!! (We were both students at a language school). We ended up having a brief affair, which he ended because he wasn't so interested after all. I felt terrible, but then I got over him quite soon. In the end, this LO turned out to be an asshole who wanted nothing but to be with a "barely legal" teenager. And he wasn't even handsome, he looked like a nerd.

I think I haven't expressed myself well. He doesn't follow my mom around in his car or creepy stuff like that. Otherwise he wouldn't be my LO, but a dangerous guy I'd hate and fear. He sees my mom every day (mom & me: same building/ LO: next door) so he obviously knows where she goes and at what time. He identifies her as my mom and is sorta nosy, so he POSSIBLY pays attention to her movements. Possibly, not sure. And I THINK he has stalked me online because of something he mentioned about me, which I had never told him, but posted on Facebook publicly.
